````math
## Appendix A Generalized Formulation for Nested Learning and Nested Systems

In this section, we discuss the generalized version of nested systems
and NSAM, we discussed in
[Section 3](#S3 "3 Nested Learning ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture"):

###### Definition 6 ((Generalized) Nested System).

A (ordered) nested system is a system with $`K`$ (ordered) levels such
that each level $`1\leq k\leq K`$ consists of a set of optimization
problems
$`\{(\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{i},\mathcal{C}^{(k)}_{i},\bm{\Theta}^{(k)}_{i})\}_{i=1}^{N_{k}}`$,
where $`\mathcal{L}_{i}(\cdot;\cdot)`$ is the optimization objective in
the $`i`$-th problem, $`\mathcal{C}_{i}`$ is its context (the data that
is optimized on), $`\bm{\Theta}_{i}`$ is the set of its parameters, and
each optimization problem is optimized using gradient descent, or
equivalently:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle{\bm{\theta}_{i}}^{(k)}_{t+1}=\arg\min_{\bm{\Phi}^{(k)}_{i}}\>\>\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{i}(\bm{\Phi}^{(k)}_{i};x_{t+1})+\frac{1}{2{\eta_{i}}^{(k)}_{t+1}}\>\|\bm{\Phi}^{(k)}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}_{i}}^{(k)}_{t}\|^{2}_{2}\qquad\text{where}\>\>x_{t+1}\thicksim\mathcal{C}^{(k)}_{i},\quad\text{and}\quad{\bm{\Phi}_{i}}^{(k)}\in\bm{\Theta}^{(k)}_{i}.`$ |  | (98) |

###### Definition 7 ((Generalized) Nested System of Associative Memories).

A nested system of associative memory (NSAM) is a system with $`K`$
(ordered) levels such that each level $`1\leq k\leq K`$ consists of a
set of optimization problems
$`\{(\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{i},\mathcal{C}^{(k)}_{i},\bm{\Theta}^{(k)}_{i})\}_{i=1}^{N_{k}}`$,
where
$`\mathcal{C}_{i}=\{(\bm{k}^{(i)}_{j},\bm{v}^{(i)}_{j})\}_{j=1}^{L_{i}}`$
is a set of ground-truth mappings,
$`\mathcal{L}_{i}(\cdot;\cdot,\cdot)`$ is the optimization objective
that measures the quality of memory learned mappings in the $`i`$-th
problem, $`\bm{\Theta}_{i}`$ is the set of memory parameters, and each
optimization problem is optimized using gradient descent:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle{\bm{\theta}_{i}}^{(k)}_{t+1}=\arg\min_{\bm{\Phi}^{(k)}_{i}}\>\>\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{i}(\bm{\Phi}^{(k)}_{i};\bm{k}^{(i)}_{t+1},\bm{v}^{(i)}_{t+1})+\frac{1}{2{\eta_{i}}^{(k)}_{t+1}}\>\|\bm{\Phi}^{(k)}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}_{i}}^{(k)}_{t}\|^{2}_{2}\quad\>\>\text{where}\>\>(\bm{k}^{(i)}_{t+1},\bm{v}^{(i)}_{t+1})\thicksim\mathcal{C}^{(k)}_{i},\>\>\>\>\text{and}\>\>\>\>{\bm{\Phi}_{i}}^{(k)}\in\bm{\Theta}^{(k)}_{i}.`$ |  | (99) |

## Appendix B Adam, AdaGrad, and Other Similar Optimizers as Associative Memory Modules

Revisiting the momentum term without using the chain rule in
backpropagation,

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | $`\displaystyle{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t+1}}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}+{\bm{m}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t+1}}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle{\bm{m}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t+1}}=\alpha_{\ell,t+1}{\bm{m}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}-\eta_{\ell,t+1}\nabla_{{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}}\mathcal{L}\left({W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}};\bm{x}_{t+1}\right),`$ |  | (100) |

one can interpret the momentum as a key or value-less associative
memory ([Behrouz et al., 2025b](#bib.bib179), see Section 5), where the
gradient terms
$`\nabla_{{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}}\mathcal{L}\left({W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}};\bm{x}_{t+1}\right)`$
are compressed into the momentum. We expect from a powerful momentum
term to perfectly memorize all the past gradients in the training
process so it can better model the current update to the weights. To
this end, one can start from defining a simple objective as:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{t}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}\|{\bm{m}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}\odot{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}-\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}\|_{2}^{2}\>\>+\>\>\lambda_{\ell}\|{\bm{m}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}\|^{2}_{F},`$ |  | (101) |

where
$`{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t+1}}=-\nabla_{{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}}\mathcal{L}\left({W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}};\bm{x}_{t+1}\right)`$.
This objective aims to find a momentum term that does not simply map the
gradients to 1 (which also results in limited memory management in
momentum), but it maps gradients to a global property of past data
samples. The more expressive this global property is, the more
accurately the momentum can incorporate the compressed information from
past. Accordingly, the objective in
[Equation 101](#A2.E101 "Equation 101 ‣ Appendix B Adam, AdaGrad, and Other Similar Optimizers as Associative Memory Modules ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture")
admits an optimal associative memory that maps gradients to
$`\bm{P}_{\ell_{t+1}}`$ as:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | $`\displaystyle{\bm{m}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}}^{*}=\left[\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\lambda_{\ell}\>\bm{I}\right)^{-1}\right]\odot\left(\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\right)=\left[\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\lambda_{\ell}\>\bm{I}\right)^{-1}\right]\odot\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}\odot\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}},\qquad\text{where}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}=\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\beta_{1}\>{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}\odot\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}=\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}\odot\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}},`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}=\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\beta_{1}\>{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}},`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}=\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}+\beta_{2}\>{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}\odot{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}=\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}+\beta_{2}\>{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}^{2}.`$ |  | (102) |

Given this solution, one can write the update step as:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{t}\>{\bm{m}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}}^{*}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{i}\>\left[\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\lambda_{\ell}\>\bm{I}\right)^{-1}\right]\odot\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}\odot\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}.`$ |  | (103) |

We start with a simple case, where $`\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}`$ is the
summation of the square of past gradients: i.e.,
$`\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bm{g}_{\ell_{i+1}}^{2}`$. With the
choice of $`\lambda\rightarrow 0`$,
[Equation 103](#A2.E103 "Equation 103 ‣ Appendix B Adam, AdaGrad, and Other Similar Optimizers as Associative Memory Modules ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture")
recovers simple gradient descent with momentum. That is, let
$`\lambda=0`$, we have:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{t}\>{\bm{m}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}}^{*}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{i}\>\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\right)^{-1}\odot\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}\odot\underset{\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}/\beta_{2}}{\underbrace{\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}}}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{t}\beta_{2}\>\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1},`$ |  | (104) |

which based on the definition of $`\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}`$,
this update rule is equivalent to gradient descent with momentum. Next,
we explore a more sophisticated design choice, where we use
$`\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}`$ as the variance of data samples before token
$`t+1`$. In this case, formally,
$`\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bm{g}_{\ell_{i+1}}^{2}}`$ and
so the update rule is as follows:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | $`\displaystyle{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{t}\>{\bm{m}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}}^{*}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{i}\>\left[\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\lambda_{\ell}\>\bm{I}\right)^{-1}\right]\odot\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}\odot\underset{\bm{H}^{(t)^{\frac{1}{2}}}_{\ell,i}/\sqrt{\beta_{2}}}{\underbrace{\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}}}\approx{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\frac{\eta_{t}}{\sqrt{\beta_{2}}}\>\frac{\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}}{\bm{H}^{(t)^{1/2}}_{\ell,i}\>+\varepsilon}`$ |  | (105) |

which is equivalent to the popular Adam optimizer ([Kingma and Ba,
2014](#bib.bib112)). Therefore, Adam is an optimal associative memory
given the $`L_{2}`$ regression objective that is defined in
[Equation 101](#A2.E101 "Equation 101 ‣ Appendix B Adam, AdaGrad, and Other Similar Optimizers as Associative Memory Modules ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture").
In fact, the update component of Adam at each state aims to learn a
mapping between the gradients and their variance (as a global property
of past data samples). One interesting point about this formulation is
about the frequency of elements. Looking at the first and second
momentum in Adam optimizer, the frequency of update for both of these
memories are the same as both are updated after each sample.
Furthermore, the computation of each of them can be done in parallel and
so are independent. Accordingly, it is one of the few examples that two
components without any internal gradient flow, are placed in the same
frequency and so level (see
[Section 3.2](#S3.SS2 "3.2 Nested Optimization Processes ‣ 3 Nested Learning ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture")).

Going beyond element-wise update, we reformulate
[Equation 101](#A2.E101 "Equation 101 ‣ Appendix B Adam, AdaGrad, and Other Similar Optimizers as Associative Memory Modules ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture")
with outer-product operation as:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{t}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}\|{\bm{m}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}-\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}\|_{2}^{2}\>\>+\>\>\lambda_{\ell}\|{\bm{m}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}\|^{2}_{F},`$ |  | (106) |

where
$`{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{t+1}}=-\nabla_{{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}}}\mathcal{L}\left({W_{\ell}}_{{}_{t}};\bm{x}_{t+1}\right)`$.
Similar to
[Equation 102](#A2.E102 "Equation 102 ‣ Appendix B Adam, AdaGrad, and Other Similar Optimizers as Associative Memory Modules ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture"),
finding the optimal solution to the above objective is defined as:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | $`\displaystyle{\bm{m}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}}^{*}=\left[\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\lambda_{\ell}\>\bm{I}\right)^{-1}\right]\left(\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\right)=\left[\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\lambda_{\ell}\>\bm{I}\right)^{-1}\right]\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}},\qquad\text{where}`$ |  | (107) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}=\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\beta_{1}\>\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}\>{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}^{\top}=\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}\>\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1},`$ |  | (108) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}=\bm{M}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\beta_{1}\>{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}^{\top},`$ |  | (109) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}=\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}+\beta_{2}\>{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}{\bm{g}_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}^{\top}.`$ |  | (110) |

With a similar choice as Adam, i.e., letting $`\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}`$ be
the variance of the gradients so far,
$`\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bm{g}_{\ell_{i+1}}\bm{g}_{\ell_{i+1}}^{\top}}`$,
then the above solution can be simplified as:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | $`\displaystyle{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i+1}}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{t}\>{\bm{m}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}}^{*}={W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\eta_{i}\>\left[\left(\bm{H}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}\>+\>\lambda_{\ell}\>\bm{I}\right)^{-1}\right]\>\underset{\bm{H}^{(t)^{\frac{1}{2}}}_{\ell,i}/\sqrt{\beta_{2}}}{\underbrace{\bm{P}_{\ell_{t}}}}\>\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i+1}\approx{W_{\ell}}_{{}_{i}}-\frac{\eta_{t}}{\sqrt{\beta_{2}}}\>\bm{H}^{(t)^{-1/2}}_{\ell,i}\>\tilde{\bm{M}}^{(t)}_{\ell,i}`$ |  | (111) |

The above formulation is the AdaGrad with momentum ([Défossez et al.,
2022](#bib.bib26)) and so generalizes the AdaGrad ([Duchi et al.,
2011](#bib.bib29)), i.e., when $`\beta_{1}=1`$. Similarly, based on the
connection of Adam optimizer ([Kingma and Ba, 2014](#bib.bib112)) with
other algorithms such as RMSProp ([Hinton et al., 2012](#bib.bib24)),
SignSGD and its momentum-based variants ([Bernstein et al.,
2018](#bib.bib25)), NAdam ([Dozat, 2016](#bib.bib23)), AMSGrad ([Reddi
et al., 2016](#bib.bib22)), RAdam ([Liu et al., 2020](#bib.bib21)), and
Lion ([Chen et al., 2023](#bib.bib20)), as well as considering AdaGrad’s
connection with optimizers such as Shampoo ([Gupta et al.,
2018](#bib.bib108)) and Soap ([Vyas et al., 2025](#bib.bib88))–i.e., as
the approximation of the preconditioning term–we can conclude that all
these optimizers can be re-formulated as associative memory that aims to
compress the gradients.

## Appendix C Delta Gradient Descent with Normalization

In
[Section 4.5](#S4.SS5 "4.5 Going Beyond Simple Gradient Descent and Momentum ‣ 4 Optimizers as Learning Modules ‣ Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture")
we discussed that gradient descent can be see as an associative memory,
and be reformulated as:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}=\arg\min_{W}\>\>\langle W\bm{x}_{t},\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t};\bm{x}_{t})\rangle+\frac{1}{2\eta_{t}}\>\|W-W_{t}\|^{2}_{2},`$ |  | (112) |

where each step aims at learning the negative of the gradient direction.
Due to the fact that this learning rule only use update terms that
depends on the current gradient, we defined
$`\mathbf{u}_{t}=-\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t};\bm{x}_{t})`$, and
extended the above process to Delta Gradient Descent with more
expressive objective of $`\mathcal{L}_{2}`$ regression loss:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}=\arg\min_{W}\>\>\frac{1}{2}\|W\bm{x}_{t}-\mathbf{u}_{t}\|^{2}_{2}+\frac{1}{2\eta_{t}}\|W-W_{t}\|^{2}_{2}.`$ |  | (113) |

We assume that $`\bm{x}_{t}`$ is normalized (e.g. in normalized memory
systems or in neural networks with normalization layers,
$`\|\bm{x}_{t}\|_{2}=\lambda`$). Taking gradient to optimize the above
objective,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle 2(W_{t+1}\bm{x}_{t}-\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t}))\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}+2\eta_{t}(W_{t+1}-W_{t})=0,`$ |  | (114) |

which results in:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}(\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}+\eta_{t}I)=\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t})\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}+\eta_{t}W_{t},`$ |  | (115) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\Rightarrow\>\>`$ | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}=(\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},x_{t})x_{t}^{\top}+\eta_{t}W_{t})(\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}+\eta_{t}I)^{-1}.`$ |  | (116) |

To compute $`(\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}+\eta_{t}I)^{-1}`$ term with
Sherman-Morrison lemma, we have:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle(x_{t}x_{t}^{\top}+\eta_{t}I)^{-1}=\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}(I-\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}+\eta_{t}}\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}),`$ |  | (117) |

and so:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  |  | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}=(\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t})\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}+\eta_{t}W_{t})\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}(I-\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}+\eta_{t}}\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top})`$ |  | (118) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\Rightarrow\>\>`$ | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}=W_{t}\left(I-\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}+\eta_{t}}\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}\right)+\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t})\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}-\underset{\frac{\lambda}{\lambda^{2}\eta_{t}+\eta^{2}_{t}}\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t})\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}}{\underbrace{\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}\eta_{t}+\eta^{2}_{t}}\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t})\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}}}`$ |  | (119) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\Rightarrow\>\>`$ | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}=W_{t}\left(I-\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}+\eta_{t}}\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}\right)-\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda^{2}\eta_{t}+\eta^{2}_{t}}-\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}\right)\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t})\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}`$ |  | (120) |
|  | $`\displaystyle\Rightarrow\>\>`$ | $`\displaystyle W_{t+1}=W_{t}\left(I-\alpha_{t}\bm{x}_{t}\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}\right)-\beta\>\>\nabla_{y_{t}}\mathcal{L}(W_{t},\bm{x}_{t})\bm{x}_{t}^{\top}`$ |  | (121) |
````
